long_biography.plain_text:
Richard Harpin's first home-assistance venture nearly failed, exhausting his savings before a direct-mail test for plumbing cover uncovered a viable model. He had learned brand building at Procter & Gamble and strategy at Deloitte, but HomeServe required a different kind of persistence. Working with South Staffs Water, he developed a subscription service that removed the uncertainty and high cost of emergency household repairs. He then expanded the model through utility partnerships and into international markets.

Brookfield's acquisition ended Harpin's HomeServe executive chapter. He now deploys his own capital through Growth Partner, backing profitable, founder-led consumer companies and pairing investment with operating support. He also owns Business Leader, whose peer groups and coaching give mid-sized business leaders access to practical guidance he lacked during HomeServe's early struggles. Growth Partner's concentrated portfolio and Business Leader's founder community place him in an active investment role rather than a passive post-sale one.
